Chapter 1 18
External ID scenarios fall under Business to Business (B2B) or Business to Consumer (B2C).
Let's consider some examples:
B2B: When organizations idx_1ce3ba1b want their employees to collaborate with business partners
and vendors on internal applications, they can use External ID for B2B collaboration.
This allows organizations to securely invite business partners and vendors as guests to
their workforce tenant. They can determine the level of access the guests have and
govern their identity lifecycle using the Entra ID Governance capabilities. For example,
if your organization is partnering with another organization on a project and needs to
collaborate with the external organization on Teams, you can invite the employees
from the external organization as business guests for easy collaboration.
B2C: When an idx_ce165445 organization wants to give access to end consumers to commercial
applications they can use Entra External ID in the external tenant. Organizations can
register their applications, customize branding, and create customized user journeys.
Typical examples include booking movie tickets, ordering groceries online, and
booking airline tickets.
Before we move on, let's understand the difference between workforce and external tenants.
In Microsoft Entra, a tenant is a dedicated idx_8d446a84 instance of Microsoft Entra ID that contains an
organization's resources like user accounts, devices, and applications. There are two ways to
configure a tenant depending on how the organization intends to use it:
A workforce tenant is a regular idx_dc584b56 Microsoft Entra tenant that contains employees,
internal business applications, and other organizational resources. In a workforce
tenant, employees idx_fd92e45e are members and external users are guests. Employees idx_63ebcaa7 and
business guests can collaborate using B2B collaboration.
An external tenant is idx_69aa54bb used exclusively for consumers. This is a idx_8d421d60 separate tenant from the
workforce tenant. It follows the standard Entra tenant model but is designed
exclusively for consumer and consumer-facing applications.

Entra External ID billing idx_4df8fc9b is based on Monthly Active Users (MAU). The first idx_ed22ddcb 50,000 MAU are
free. Each user who authenticates to the tenant once a month contributes to the MAU.
Entra External ID is discussed in detail in Chapters 12 and 13.
Global Secure Access
The way of working has changed. The days when people worked in traditional offices are long
gone. Today, people work from idx_9d60f928 anywhere. As applications and data move to cloud, security
threats increase. The modern way of working demands more than perimeter security. An
identity-aware cloud-delivered security solution is the need of the hour. This new security idx_2f683beb
category is called Secure Services Edge (SSE).
Microsoft's SSE solution idx_89a94f3a is called Global Secure Access (GSA). This is a unifying term used idx_8ff0abb3 for
Microsoft Entra Internet Access and Microsoft Entra Private Access. GSA is idx_d290351a built on core
zero trust principles. The following idx_01bd8969 picture shows these components:

Microsoft Entra Internet Access and Microsoft Entra Private Access, together with Microsoft
Defender for Cloud Apps (Microsoft's cloud-focused Cloud Access Security Broker), converge
network, identity, and endpoint access idx_438dcd64 controls to help organizations protect any application
or resource from anywhere. Microsoft Entra ID simplifies policy management and enables
secure employee access to any cloud or on-premises workloads.
GSA streamlines the roll-out and management of access control capabilities using Microsoft's
network spanning 70 regions and more than 190 network edge locations.
Microsoft Entra Internet Access
Microsoft Entra Internet Access provides idx_0b85eacb secure access to internet and SaaS applications idx_703984ec with
an identity-based Secure Web Gateway (SWG). It can acquire network idx_6536e3b3 traffic either from the
user's desktop or from a remote location like a branch office. It is context aware, and uses
information like user, device, location, and risk to apply Conditional Access policies. It idx_4540e480 enables
web-content filtering based on web content categories or Fully Qualified Domain Names
(FQDN).
21 Introduction to Microsoft Entra
Microsoft Entra Internet Access for Microsoft Services
This service provides direct connectivity idx_99b832ef to Microsoft Services, improving security and
performance. Using this service, organizations can connect to Microsoft services directly from a
desktop or branch location. Universal Tenant Restrictions can be idx_1000eae3 applied to reduce the risk of
data exfiltration to unauthorized accounts or tenants. It offers improved threat detection with
source IP restoration for Entra ID sign-in logs.
Microsoft Entra Internet Access will be covered in Chapter 14, Microsoft Entra Internet Access.
Microsoft Entra Private Access
Using Microsoft Entra Private idx_b0e312ea Access, organizations can provide users secure access to private,
corporate resources without a Virtual Private Network (VPN). It builds on idx_7b08b102 Microsoft Entra
application proxy and offers per-app adaptive access using Conditional Access policies that
provide more granular security than a VPN. Microsoft Entra Private Access provides zero-trust
access to a range of IP addresses or FQDNs idx_63da60a0 using a feature called Quick Access. Organizations
can modernize authentication to legacy applications using its integration with Conditional
Access and provide a seamless experience to end users by acquiring network traffic from
desktops. It can work side-by-side with existing non-Microsoft SSE solutions.
Microsoft Entra Private Access will be covered in Chapter 15, Microsoft Entra Private Access.
Licensing
Both Microsoft Entra Internet idx_6618d5f1 Access and Microsoft Entra Private Access can be bought as

chunks.heading: Chapter 1 20
chunks.content:
standalone products or as a part of Entra Suite. Organizations that choose to buy these
products as standalone must have at least Microsoft Entra ID P1 licenses.
Microsoft Entra Internet Access for Microsoft services capabilities are included in Microsoft
Entra ID P1 or P2 licenses.
Summary
In this chapter, we learned the basics of identity and identity and access management. We also
discussed the common authentication and authorization standards. Additionally, we learned
about the Microsoft identity platform and how it supports application developers. Lastly, this
chapter introduced the Microsoft Entra suite of products, their basic features, and licensing.
The rest of the chapters in this book will build upon the content of this chapter. In the next
chapter, we will learn the fundamentals of Microsoft Entra ID such as SSO, MFA,
authentication methods, and Conditional Access.

2
Fundamentals of Microsoft Entra
ID
Microsoft Entra ID is an identity and access management solution intended for enterprise
environments. Its main purpose is to provide secure and streamlined access to resources,
applications, and services, whether on-premises or in the cloud. Organizations can use Entra
ID to authenticate users, manage permissions, and enforce policies aimed at protecting
sensitive data from unauthorized access. Conditional Access enables administrators to
implement access controls based on user identity, device status, or location. Multifactor
authentication is available as an additional security measure, requiring more than just
passwords for access. The platform also offers SSO capabilities, allowing users to access
different applications and services efficiently.
This chapter will cover:
Microsoft Entra roles
Single Sign-On (SSO) and Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA)
Authentication methods
Conditional access
Protected actions
These topics are essential to understanding the more complex topics that the rest of the book
will cover.
•
•
•
•
•
Microsoft Entra roles
Microsoft Entra idx_c3254d45 follows the role-based access control (RBAC) model. RBAC assigns
permissions based on specific roles, ensuring users have access only to the idx_8da91440 resources required
for their duties. This minimizes security risks by restricting unauthorized access. Microsoft
Entra roles control access to Microsoft Entra resources like users, groups, devices, and
applications using the Microsoft Graph API.
It is important to understand how Microsoft Entra ID determines if a user has access to a
resource. This information will be useful when troubleshooting access issues. The following
are the high-level steps:
A user acquires a token for the Microsoft Graph endpoint
The user makes an API call to Microsoft Entra ID via Microsoft Graph using the issued
token
Microsoft Entra ID either evaluates the user's role memberships based on the claims in
the user's access token or retrieves all role assignments that apply to the user directly
or through group memberships to the resource on which the action is being taken
Microsoft Entra ID determines if the action in the API call is allowed in the roles that
this user has on the resource. If it is allowed, the access is granted; otherwise, it is
denied.
Microsoft Entra offers the following types of roles.

Built-in roles idx_bd4b2483 are out-of-the-box roles with a predefined set of permissions. These roles cannot
be modified. There are several built-in roles in Microsoft Entra and new ones are regularly
added by Microsoft. Built-in roles are available with the Microsoft Entra ID Free plan. To view
the built-in roles in Microsoft Entra, follow these steps:
Log in to https://entra.microsoft.com and in the left navigation menu navigate to

For most organizations, the built-in roles meet their requirements. Organizations that have
more granular idx_5e4dfcec or sophisticated requirements can create custom roles. A custom role is a

Assigning roles
Users need idx_4e827678 to be assigned roles for them to be able to perform tasks on Microsoft Entra
resources. This is done by creating a role assignment. A role assignment ties a role definition to a
security principal at a scope level. These terms are explained as follows:
Security principal: The identity that gets the permissions defined in the role. This
could be a user, group, or a service principal.

Role definition: A role is also called a role definition. It is either a built-in or custom
role.
Scope: A group of Microsoft Entra resources on which the role definition provides
permissions. For example, the entire tenant, an Administrative Unit, or a specific
Microsoft Entra resource such as a group or application.
For example, a role assignment could grant a user the App Registration Administrator role only
for specific applications.
There are multiple options to assign roles in Microsoft Entra as described next.
Assigning directly to users
This is the idx_a5273e48 default way of assigning roles. Both built-in and custom roles can be assigned
directly to users.
Using role-assignable groups
Using this idx_219bfb60 method you create role-assignable groups and assign roles to the groups. Assigning
roles to groups makes administration easier than assigning roles to individual users.
To add roles to a group, create a new security or Microsoft 365 group with the
isAssignableToRole property set to true. A role-assignable group has the following
restrictions:
The isAssignableToRole property cannot be changed once the group is created.
You cannot make an already existing group a role-assignable group.
A role-assignable group cannot have dynamic membership. The members must be
manually assigned.
Another group cannot be added as a member of a role-assignable group.
A maximum of 500 role-assignable groups can be created in a single tenant.
A Microsoft Entra P1 license is required to create and use role-assignable groups.

chunks.content:
Chapter 2 34
Single sign-on
Companies create and host web applications and make them available to users to be accessed
as a service. Users idx_7193e33e access these applications using a browser. Single Sign-On (SSO) makes it
possible for users to navigate between these applications without having to enter credentials
multiple times. Instead of remembering and entering separate usernames and passwords for
each application, users log in once and gain entry to all interconnected systems without
further prompts. This approach streamlines user experience by reducing password fatigue and
enhances productivity and security.
Microsoft Entra ID application gallery has several applications that can be configured for SSO.
There are several idx_df0a945f SSO options to choose from depending on the needs of the organization. They
are listed as follows:
Federation: When SSO is idx_89cc314b set up to work between multiple identity providers (IdPs), it
is called federation. Federation improves security, reliability, and end-user experience.
With federated SSO, users use their Microsoft Entra account to authenticate.
Federation is supported for SAML 2.0, WS-Fed, and OIDC applications. It is the richest
method of SSO and is recommended over other SSO methods like password-based SSO.
Password: This method is primarily used for on-premises applications that are
configured idx_41b302e4 to use Microsoft Entra Application Proxy. In this method, the user signs
into the application using their password for the first time. For subsequent login
attempts, Entra ID provides the user credentials to the application. This enables secure
password storage and replay using a web browser extension or mobile application.
Linked: This method provides a consistent user experience for organizations that are in
the process of migrating applications to Entra ID. In this method, once the user
authenticates with a linked application, a user account needs to be created before SSO
can be provided. This account can be created either manually or automatically. The
user can see links for all linked applications in their MyApps portal. Conditional Access
policies or MFA cannot be used as the linked application does not provide SSO through
Entra ID.
Integrated Windows Authentication (IWA): Microsoft Application Proxy can be used
to provide SSO for applications that use Integrated Windows Authentication. These
applications require a Kerberos ticket.
Header-based: Microsoft Entra application proxy supports SSO for applications that
use headers for authentication. Header values are configured in Microsoft Entra ID
based on application requirements. These values are then sent to the application via
•
•
•
•
•
35 Fundamentals of Microsoft Entra ID
application proxy. This helps organizations to replace VPNs and remove dependencies

chunks.title: masteringmicrosoftentraid
chunks.heading: Chapter 2 34
chunks.content:
on on-premises infrastructure.
How SSO is implemented depends on where the application is hosted. This matters because
hosting affects the way traffic is routed to access the application. For example, users don't need
internet access to access an on-premises application but need it to access an application hosted
on the cloud.
As you plan your SSO deployment, consider the following points.
Administrative roles
Adhering to the zero-trust principle, it is advisable to assign roles with the minimum necessary
permissions idx_575bf233 for each task. Carefully assess the available Microsoft Entra roles and select the
most appropriate one for each application persona. Certain roles may only be needed on a
temporary basis.
Certificates
When SAML applications are federated with Entra ID, a certificate is created that is valid for
three years idx_9cd8a658 by default. The expiration date can be customized if needed. It is important to
document and manage the certificate renewal process to ensure that there are no unforeseen
outages due to certificate expiry. Identify the right people who should be involved in managing
the certificate lifecycle.
Communication
It is important to set up a proper communication process to proactively inform the relevant
stakeholders idx_9944a3bd of any upcoming changes. Identify the relevant stakeholders, including end users
of the application, and the process by which they should be informed of upcoming changes
and available support options.
Licensing
Typically, the idx_144c261c following licenses are required:
Microsoft Entra ID: SSO is free for applications already integrated with Entra ID.
Additional licenses may be required if you wish to deploy advanced features.
Application licensing: Some applications require that all users who access the
application be assigned appropriate licenses. Check with your application owner to
ensure compliance with license requirements.
Shared accounts
Some applications idx_95863444 allow the use of shared accounts. From an Entra perspective, there is no
difference between applications that use shared accounts and applications that use individual
•
•

user accounts. Some additional care may need to be taken while deploying an application that
uses shared accounts. The following are some best practices:
Document the sets of users who should have access to the application and the
credentials associated with each set.
Create and use a security group to manage users in each set.
Change the password of the shared account. Once the application is deployed, users
don't idx_bcdbb3c4 need the password of the shared account. The password is stored in Entra ID and
should be long and complex.
Consider configuring automatic password rollover.
SSO deployment options
There are several ways to configure SSO for applications, depending on the authentication
method idx_d69d745c they use. Cloud applications typically support OIDC, OAuth, SAML, password-based,
or linked SSO. On-premises applications, on the other hand, may rely on password-based,
Integrated Windows Authentication, header-based, or linked SSO. To enable SSO for on-
premises apps, Microsoft Entra Application Proxy must be configured.

Based on this flowchart, you can determine the most appropriate SSO method for your

Multi-factor authentication
As covered in Chapter 1, Introduction to Microsoft Entra, multi-factor authentication (MFA) is
an idx_bdf74f6f enhanced security feature that requires the user to present a combination of two or more
forms of authentication methods from the following list:
Something you know, like a PIN or password
Something you have, like a hardware security token
Something you are, like a biometric
Administrators can decide the second factor to challenge the user with. There are several
verification methods to choose from like Microsoft Authenticator app, Passkeys, hardware, and
software tokens, and certificates. Once the administrator enables the second factor
authentication, users will be asked to register for it at next logon. On subsequent logons, they
will be able to satisfy the MFA conditions to complete login.
Microsoft Entra idx_9f64928c MFA also provides for secure password reset. When users register for MFA,
they can also register for self-service password reset (SSPR).
Microsoft Entra MFA processes and stores personal and organizational information in
datacenters in the United States, Europe, and Asia Pacific. Microsoft Entra MFA stores bypassed
users, Microsoft Authenticator device token change requests, MFA activity reports, and MFA
activation for 90 days. Personal data like usernames, phone numbers, and IP addresses are not
stored. Log data is stored for 30 days. Tenant settings like account lockout thresholds,
notifications, and phone call settings might also be stored.

Chapter 2 38
Configuring prompts and session lifetime
There are idx_4ca5d6d7 several settings that determine how often a user will need to reauthenticate to
Microsoft Entra ID. This can involve only the first factor or the second factor as well. The
default setting for user sign-in frequency is a rolling 90-day window. Organizations can choose
to change this to suit their requirements. The following settings are recommended by
Microsoft:
Organizations with Entra ID P1 or P2 license:
Enable SSO across applications
Use Microsoft Entra Conditional Access Sign-in frequency policy to enable
reauthentication
Limit sign-in duration for users who sign in from unmanaged devices
Organizations with Entra ID Free license:
Enable SSO across applications
Enable the Stay signed in? option
Ensure mobile users have the Microsoft Authenticator app to broker into other
Microsoft Entra ID federated apps
Without session lifetime settings, each time a user closes and reopens the browser they are
asked idx_2ee864ed to reauthenticate. This is because the browser has no persistent cookie. In Office clients,
the default is a 90-day rolling window. If a user is inactive for 90 days, they will be asked for
first and second factor authentication. If there are multiple settings defining session lifetime,
the most restrictive one applies. For example, if you have both the following settings enabled,
the user will need to reauthenticate every 14 days.
Show option to remain signed in
Remember MFA for 14 days
To configure the option to remain signed in follow these steps:
Sign in to https://entra.microsoft.com as a Global Administrator.
In the left pane, navigate to Users | User settings.
In the right pane, toggle the Show keep user signed in to Yes.

Authentication methods
Microsoft Entra idx_2f219939 ID offers several authentication methods, ranging from simple passwords to
MFA methods like SMS and tokens, and even passwordless solutions like Windows Hello for
Business and passkeys. Microsoft recommends passwordless authentication as the most secure
method of authentication and the best user sign-in experience. The following figure shows the
various authentication methods available in Microsoft Entra ID:
Figure 2.17: Microsoft Entra ID authentication methods
Some of these authentication methods can be used for both MFA and SSPR. Users can register
for both MFA and idx_c1ead0d7 SSPR in a single step. It is recommended that users register for more than
one method so if one is not available, they can use the other one. Some of these methods like
FIDO security keys can be used as the primary method. Others are only available as a
secondary method.
These authentication methods can be managed using the Authentication methods policy in
the Microsoft Entra admin center. The Authentication Policy Administrator role is required
to manage this policy. Once an authentication method is enabled in the policy, it can be used
both for MFA and SSPR. The Authentication strengths feature in Conditional Access provides
more control over which method can be used in which scenario.
Let's now discuss each of these authentication methods in detail.
Temporary Access Pass
When a new employee joins the organization, the IT admin creates a user account for them and
assigns idx_f55b62ff a temporary password. Usually, this idx_45ad6cdc password is the same for all new user accounts
45 Fundamentals of Microsoft Entra ID
and it is shared with the new employee using insecure channels like personal email accounts.
This poses obvious security concerns. Instead of issuing a standard password, administrators
can use a Temporary Access Pass (TAP), which is a time-limited code. The TAP can be
configured for use once or multiple times. TAP brings users one step closer to being
passwordless by enabling simple onboarding to passwordless methods like passkeys and
Microsoft Authenticator app sign in. It also simplifies account recovery.
The following steps explain creating and using TAP:

Administrator.

Now let's discuss the various passwordless methods available with Microsoft Entra ID.
Passwordless authentication
MFA helps idx_1f6f2a47 secure the organization, but it idx_e56064f6 also causes users to get frustrated if they must
answer frequent MFA prompts. Passwordless methods completely eliminate the need for
passwords, offer a more user-friendly experience by removing the need to remember and
change passwords, and satisfy MFA requirements. Microsoft Entra ID offers several
passwordless sign-in methods. Let's explore them.
Windows Hello for Business
Windows Hello for Business is a passwordless authentication method using which users can
sign into idx_6d2adeb1 Windows devices using biometrics idx_62fa801c such as facial recognition or fingerprint or a PIN,
instead of a password. It is a phishing-resistant, two-factor authentication that has brute-force
49 Fundamentals of Microsoft Entra ID
protection built in. When used with FIDO/WebAuthN, Windows Hello for Business can also be
used to sign into various websites, thus eliminating the need to remember multiple passwords.
Windows idx_7b29d027 Hello for Business offers the following benefits:
It protects against credential theft. An attacker must have both the device and the PIN
to gain access.
Since no passwords are used, it circumvents phishing and brute force attacks. It also
prevents server breaches and replay attacks, as credentials are asymmetric and
generated idx_92fdfb64 within the Trusted Platform Module (TPM).
The PIN can only be used with the device it was configured with. So even if an attacker
knows the PIN, they will still need the device to access the data. Moreover, Windows
Hello for Business has brute-force protection built in.
Windows Hello for Business uses a two-factor authentication that combines device-specific
credentials with a biometric. The credential is tied to Microsoft Entra ID. During provisioning,
Windows idx_a1f011ec Hello is set up on the device and the user is asked to provide idx_0eee73cc a gesture that will be
used to verify their identity and unlock the device. The biometric data is stored on the
Windows device making it impossible to steal as it never leaves the device.
Windows Hello for Business supports facial recognition, fingerprint scanning, and iris
recognition. Major hardware vendors are now shipping hardware devices that are compatible
with Windows Hello for Business.
The following steps describe how the sign-in process works:
When a user signs into their Windows device using biometric or PIN, it unlocks their
Windows idx_01111df7 Hello for Business private key. This key is then securely transmitted to the

chunks.title: masteringmicrosoftentraid
chunks.heading: Chapter 2 48
chunks.content:
Cloud Authentication Provider (CloudAP).
The CloudAP requests a nonce from Microsoft Entra ID. A nonce is a random number
that can be used once and is valid for 5 minutes.
Once it receives the nonce from Microsoft Entra ID, the CloudAP signs it with the user's
private key and sends it back to Microsoft Entra ID.
Microsoft idx_16507b6d Entra ID uses the user's public key to validate the nonce. It then creates a
Primary Refresh Token (PRT) using the session key, which is encrypted with the
device's transport key and sends it back to CloudAP.
CloudAP leverages idx_bb0c4a61 the device's private transport key to securely receive the session key,
which is then protected by the device's Trusted Platform Module (TPM).
The CloudAP informs Windows that the authentication was successful. The user can
now log in to Windows and get SSO access to cloud and on-premises applications.

Windows Hello for Business provides secure, passwordless authentication using device-
specific credentials and biometrics, enabling users to access Windows devices and cloud
resources with enhanced protection against phishing and brute-force attacks.
Platform Credential for macOS
Platform Credential for macOS leverages Microsoft Enterprise Single Sign-On Extension
(SSOe) to provide idx_76d1793a enhanced security. It establishes idx_7ba9a81b a secure enclave supported by a hardware-
bound cryptographic key, which facilitates single sign-on for applications that authenticate
using Microsoft Entra ID. Users still need to sign in to macOS using the local account and
password. Using this method, users can go passwordless. Users may utilize Touch ID to unlock
their device, and employ phishing-resistant credentials that are compliant with Windows
Hello for Business. This helps customers eliminate security keys and implement zero trust.
Platform Credential for macOS may serve as a phishing-resistant solution for WebAuthn
challenges, including idx_787cd535 scenarios such as browser re-authentication. This uses the Passkey
(FIDO2) authentication method.
Platform SSO on macOS with SmartCard
This idx_5888a78f method allows idx_d0fc1829 users to go passwordless on Mac devices by using external smart cards or
smart-card compatible hardware tokens like YubiKey. After the device is unlocked, the smart
card utilizes Microsoft Entra ID to provide SSO capabilities across idx_918b98ee applications. This method
uses certificate-based authentication (CBA). Platform SSO can be configured using
Microsoft Intune or idx_29a20298 any other Mobile Device Management (MDM) solution.
Microsoft Authenticator
Many organizations already use the Microsoft Authenticator app as an MFA method. It is also a
convenient idx_af9a0b61 method to help organizations implement passwordless. Using this, users can sign
in to any platform or application by approving a notification idx_8435b306 on their phone or matching a
number displayed on the screen. Biometrics like face or fingerprint or a PIN can be used to
validate the user's identity. Passwordless authentication with Microsoft Authenticator follows
a similar process to Windows Hello for Business. The primary distinction is that user
identification is required so Entra ID can locate the appropriate Authenticator app and
determine its version. The following steps describe the authentication flow:
On the computer, the user enters their username on the application they want to
access.
Microsoft idx_900acd83 Entra ID detects that the user idx_37e6de5c is registered for passwordless. Depending on
the device, it sends a notification to the app via Apple Push Notification Service
(APNS) or Firebase Cloud Messaging (FCM).
The user receives the push notification and opens the app, which then calls Microsoft

Passkey (FIDO2) authentication
Passkeys, developed idx_37d436c5 by the FIDO (Fast Identity Online) Alliance, offer an innovative approach
to secure authentication. They eliminate the need for traditional idx_1481e68c passwords by leveraging
FIDO2 standards. These keys depend on public key cryptography to authenticate identities,
offering a idx_86d97b41 higher level of security by minimizing vulnerabilities such as phishing, password-
related breaches, and weak passwords. By replacing passwords with cryptographic credentials,
passkeys simplify the sign-in process while enhancing protection against cyber threats.
Passkeys are supported on modern systems like Windows 10 (version 1903 or higher) and are
integrated into tools like the Microsoft Authenticator, empowering organizations to adopt
robust, password-free security solutions.
As per idx_857953d7 the FIDO2 specification, each security key vendor must provide an Authenticator
Attestation GUID (AAGUID). The AAGUID is a 128-bit identifier that specifies the key type.
Passkey providers on desktops and mobiles are also expected to provide an AAGUID during
registration. Before enabling passkeys, ensure that the following requirements have been met:
Microsoft Entra multifactor authentication should be enabled in the organization.
Users should have the Microsoft Authenticator app installed on their devices.
User devices should support passkey authentication. The following devices are
supported:
Entra ID idx_088cbeb3 joined devices should be running Windows 10 version 1903 or higher.
Hybrid idx_a9e177e2 joined devices should be running Windows 10 version 2004 or higher.

This method is idx_740474be useful for frontline workers that use shared devices. Users can use a unique idx_5146e183 QR
code and a PIN for secure sign-in. The QR code is unique for each user, and it can be
downloaded from Microsoft Entra admin center and printed on the user's badge for ease of
use. QR code is a single-factor authentication method. The following steps enable users to use
QR code authentication:
Log in to https://entra.microsoft.com with an account that has the Authentication
Policy Administrator role assigned.
Navigate to Entra ID | Authentication methods | Policies.
In the right pane, click on QR code and click on Enable. Select the groups to include or
exclude from the policy.
